raw_response:
I’m 66 now, and I don’t change things just for the sake of changing them. On 9 mu, with only two people in the house, I need a plan that is steady, not too labor-heavy, and not too risky. So I’ll keep most of the land in the usual wheat-maize rotation because that gives me grain income twice and spreads the risk. I’ll still keep some cotton because I know how to manage it, and if grain prices are weak, cotton can still help balance the year. Since I have well irrigation, I won’t chase the maximum yield with excessive water and fertilizer, but I also won’t cut inputs too far. At my age, I pay attention to return per mu and labor timing. Wheat needs to stay stable, maize must go in quickly right after wheat harvest, and cotton I’ll keep on a smaller area because it takes more hands during the season and at picking.

For wheat, I’ll use the better field and manage it in the familiar way: base fertilizer before sowing, then one topdress at jointing, with three irrigations if the season is normal. For summer maize on that same land, I’ll plant immediately after wheat harvest with a hybrid seed, do one main basal application and one light topdress, and usually irrigate once unless summer rain is good. Cotton I’ll keep lighter in area, use improved seed, and feed it in splits because one-time heavy fertilizer is wasteful on my land. I’m aiming for a dependable year, not an aggressive one.
